title: Choose the nature world
question: Research-lab structure stays. The roll landed on a field survey: soft topographic contour lines as the organic texture. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Field Survey
options.lineage: Naturalist field-station surveys and topographic maps
options.thesis: Each post is a surveyed site; soft contour lines drawn like terrain give heroes and bands their organic texture while posts stay clean.
options.viewport: Index hero sits on a pale lichen field crossed by soft contour lines rising around the robot logo, then the post list on a clean band.
options.risk: Contour lines read as stock topo wallpaper if they spread past heroes and bands.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Soft hatching densities and translucent overlapping sheets become the texture.
options.case: Fuses partly: hatching can render in soft greens, but the darkroom grammar reads technical rather than natural.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: One continuous ribbon threads through dated posts like an object's custody history.
options.case: Fuses poorly because its archival buff and red silk fight the soft green brief, and posts aren't a custody chain.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Soft cumulus masses and sky voids give the page an atmospheric, weathered texture.
options.case: Fuses poorly because it reads sky and dream rather than green nature, and volumetric effects distract from reading.

canonCard.label: Sage research journal
canonCard.thesis: The research-lab journal in a soft sage palette with gentle paper grain, played straight.
canonCard.viewport: Quiet header, sage-tinted hero with title and lede, then the post list.
canonCard.risk: Nature reads mostly through color; the texture stays faint.
